claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength near 423 MPa at 30% strain and 1273 K.
Adding a minor amount of Y2O3 during powder processing can establish a uniform dispersion of fine oxide nanoparticles in the BCC matrix after consolidation and heat treatment.
The introduced Y2O3 nanoparticles will be stable at elevated temperature.
Controlled oxygen levels promote the formation of well-dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles in powder-processed TiVNbTa.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as pinning centers against dislocation motion.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
The nanoparticle dispersion stabilizes the TiVNbTa microstructure at high temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion and microstructural stabilization reduce creep and high-temperature softening.
The oxide dispersion delays the onset of plasticity at elevated temperature.
The Y2O3-modified TiVNbTa alloy will have a yield strength above 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The expected strength improvement will better meet the mechanical requirements of an intermediate heat-transfer layer between W and CuCrZr.
Testing at 1273 K under loading up to 30% strain represents the relevant intermediate-layer service conditions.
The magnitude of the yield-strength improvement depends on nanoparticle size, distribution, and volume fraction.
